312 – 13 × 14 + 207 ÷ 4 = 539
questions.solution:
Given Equation: 312 – 13 × 14 + 207 ÷ 4 = 539

BODMAS Rule:

Let's check each Option One by One:

Option 1) ÷ and –

Given: 312 – 13 × 14 + 207 ÷ 4 = 539

After interchanging the numbers we get;

312 ÷13 × 14 + 207 - 4 = 539

24 × 14 + 207 - 4 = 539

336 + 207 - 4 = 539

543 - 4 = 539

539 = 539.

Option 2) – and +

Given: 312 – 13 × 14 + 207 ÷ 4 = 539

After interchanging the numbers we get;

312 + 13 × 14 - 207 ÷ 4 = 539

312 + 13 × 14 - 51.75 = 539

312 + 182 - 51.75 = 539

494 - 51.75 = 539

442.25 ≠ 539.

Option 3) ÷ and +

Given: 312 – 13 × 14 + 207 ÷ 4 = 539

After interchanging the numbers we get;

312 – 13 × 14 ÷ 207 + 4 = 539

312 – 13 × 0.06 + 4 = 539

312 - 0.87 + 4 = 539

316 - 0.87 = 539

315.13 ≠ 539.

Option 4) + and ×

Given: 312 – 13 × 14 + 207 ÷ 4 = 539

After interchanging the numbers we get;

312 – 13 + 14 × 207 ÷ 4 = 539

312 – 13 + 14 × 51.75 = 539

312 – 13 + 724.5 = 539

1036.5 – 13 = 539

1023.5 ≠ 539.

Hence, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.

questions.question: Which committee recommended the formation of a new category of NBFC i.e., Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institution?
questions.questionHtml: Which committee recommended the formation of a new category of NBFC i.e., Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Malegam Committee.

Key Points

  • The creation of a separate category for NBFCs operating in the microfinance sector (NBFC-MFI) was done based on the recommendations of the Malegam Committee.
  • The Malegam Committee was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 2010 to review the microfinance sector in India and provide recommendations for its growth and development.
  • The committee recommended the creation of a separate category of NBFCs for microfinance to regulate and supervise them effectively, and to ensure that they comply with the prescribed norms and standards.
  • The NBFC-MFIs are required to obtain a certificate of registration from the RBI and comply with the regulations on interest rates, lending practices, borrower protection, and reporting requirements.

Additional Information

  • Shah Committee: This committee was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India in 1989 to review the working of the monetary system in India and to suggest measures for its improvement.
  • Kamath Committee: This committee was appointed by the Reserve Bank of India in 2014 to review the working of the asset reconstruction companies in India and to suggest measures for their improvement.

questions.question: Harrod Domar growth model is known for highlighting the role of savings and investments. Which Five-Year Plan in India was based on this model?

  • First Five-Year Plan
    • 1st five-year plan was from 1951 to 1956.
    • The prime target of the first five-year plan of India was the Development of agriculture.
    • The target Growth was 2.1 % and the Actual Growth was 3.6 %.
    • It was based on Harrod-Domar.

  • The second five-year plan is based on the so-called Mahalanobis model.
  • This was the USSR model Indianized by PC Mahalanobis, the founder of the Indian Statistical Institute and a close aide of Nehru.
  • This model is known to have set the statistical foundations for state-directed investments and created the intellectual underpinnings of the license-raj through an elaborate input-output model.
  • This Model suggested that there should be an emphasis on the heavy industries, which can lead the Indian Economy to a long-term higher growth path
  • Started Industrial Policy Resolution 1956.

Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966)

  • The Third 5 year Plan focused on agriculture & enhancement in the production of wheat, but the succinct Sino - Indian War in the year 1962 exposed flaws in the economy & shifted the spotlight towards the Defence industry.
  • On May 31 & June 1, 1961, the National Development Council considered the Draft Report on the Third Plan and generally approved it.
  • In the course of this period, India's economy must not only enlarge swiftly but must, in unison, become independent and self-generating.
  • This long-standing approach is projected to offer a wide-ranging design of expansion for the country's natural resources, industrial advance, and agricultural changes in the social structure & an incorporated scheme of regional & national development.

Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-1974)

  • The fourth Five Year Plan was the first plan launched by the Indira Gandhi government amid the pressure of drought, devaluation, and inflationary recession.
  • The country was fighting with population explosion, increased unemployment, poverty, and a shackling economy. In addition, the situation in East Pakistan (now independent Bangladesh) was becoming dire as the Indo-Pakistani War of 1971 and the Bangladesh Liberation War took place.
  • Funds earmarked for industrial development had to be used for the war effort.

questions.question: Fundamental duties are ________ and not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
questions.questionHtml: Fundamental duties are ________ and not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is statutory.

Key Points

  • Fundamental duties come under Part IVA and Article 51A.
  • These duties are statutory and are not enforceable by law but are taken into account by the courts while adjudicating any matter.
  • Fundamental Duties in the Constitution are inspired by USSR.
  • Japan is the only democratic country, other than India, to have Fundamental duties in its Constitution.
  • These duties were incorporated through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 in the Constitution on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee. 
  • Only 8 Fundamental duties were based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendation while the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act added 10 Fundamental duties in the Constitution.
  • Later, the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 was passed that introduced one more fundamental duty in the Constitution. Now there are Eleven Fundamental duties in the Constitution.
  • Rights and duties are correlative and inseparable.

Additional Information

List of Fundamental Duties of India

  • It shall be the duty of every citizen of India —
  1. To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem;
  2. To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom;
  3. To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
  4. To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so;
  5. To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women;
  6. To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture;
  7. To protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife and to have compassion for living creatures;
  8. To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform;
  9. To safeguard public property and to abjure violence;
  10. To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement;
  11. Who is a parent or guardian, to provide opportunities for education to his child, or as the case may be, ward between the age of six to fourteen years.

questions.question: When did Dmitri Mendeleev invent the periodic table, ordering the symbols of the chemical elements according to their atomic weights?
questions.questionHtml: When did Dmitri Mendeleev invent the periodic table, ordering the symbols of the chemical elements according to their atomic weights?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1869.

Key Points

  • Dmitri Mendeleev invented the periodic table in 1869, organizing elements based on their atomic weights and properties.
  • Mendeleev left gaps in the table for elements yet to be discovered, predicting their properties accurately.
  • On March 6, 1869, Mendeleev presented his first periodic table to the Russian Chemical Society.
  • Mendeleev’s table demonstrated that when elements are arranged by increasing atomic weight, certain chemical properties repeat periodically.
  • This periodic arrangement became the foundation for the modern periodic table used in chemistry today.

Additional Information

  • Periodic Law: Mendeleev’s periodic table was based on the periodic law which states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their atomic weights.
  • Modern Periodic Table: Today, the periodic table is organized by atomic number (proton count) rather than atomic weight, as introduced by Henry Moseley in 1913.
  • Predicted Elements: Mendeleev accurately predicted the existence and properties of elements like germanium (eka-silicon), gallium (eka-aluminum), and scandium.
  • Contributors to Periodicity: Other scientists like John Newlands (law of octaves) and Lothar Meyer worked on periodic classification, but Mendeleev’s table was more comprehensive and widely accepted.
  • Significance: Mendeleev’s periodic table provided a systematic framework for studying chemical elements, aiding in the discovery of new elements and advancing the field of chemistry.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Henry Chandler Cowles.Key Points 

  • Henry Chandler Cowles studied ecological succession in the Indiana Dunes of Northwest Indiana in the 1890s.
  • Henry Chandler Cowles (1869-1939) was a University of Chicago botany professor and conservationist, his studies of plant life in the Indiana Dunes made Cowles one of America's most notable early ecologists.
  • In 1896, Cowles traveled to the southern shore of Lake Michigan to see the Indiana Dunes for the first time and studied them.
  • His study explained the development and distribution of local plant communities in terms of topography, moisture, wind, erosion, sedimentation, and other geological processes.

questions.question: The layer of earth that separates the crust from the core is:
questions.questionHtml: The layer of earth that separates the crust from the core is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mantle.

Key Points

The mantle: 

  • The mantle extends up to a depth of 2900 km below the crust.
  • It separates the crust from the core.
  • The upper part of the mantle is known as the asthenosphere.
  • Nearly 84% of the earth’s volume and 67% of the earth’s mass is occupied by the mantle.
  • The major constituent elements of the mantle are Silicon and Magnesium and hence it is also termed as SIMA.

Additional InformationThe crust:

  • The crust is the uppermost layer over the earth’s surface.
  • It is the thinnest layer.
  • it is only about 5 km on the ocean floors, which mainly consists of silica and alumina thus called sial (si-silica and al-alumina), and 35 km on the continental masses, which mainly consists of silica and alumina.

The core:

  • The innermost layer is the core with a radius of about 3500 km and divided into Inner and Outer core.
  • It is called nife (ni – nickel and fe – ferrous – iron) as it's mainly made up of nickel and iron.
  • Central core is called the Inner core and has a very high temperature and pressure.

questions.question: Iron age is so named because during this time iron mostly replaced _________ in implements and weapons, beginning in the Middle East and South-eastern Europe.
questions.questionHtml: Iron age is so named because during this time iron mostly replaced _________ in implements and weapons, beginning in the Middle East and South-eastern Europe.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is bronze.

Key Points

  • The Iron Age is a period in human history characterized by the widespread use of iron tools and weapons.
  • This period began around 1200 BCE in the Middle East and gradually spread to other parts of the world.
  • Before the Iron Age, bronze was the preferred material for making tools and weapons.
  • Bronze is an alloy made from copper and tin.​

Additional Information

  • The most significant development was the use of iron for tools, weapons, and agricultural implements.
  • Iron is stronger and more durable than bronze, the dominant material of the preceding era.
  • Iron led to advancements in agriculture, construction, and warfare. For example, iron plowshares improved farming efficiency, while iron weapons gave rise to powerful warrior classes.
  • The Iron Age saw the transition from small tribal settlements to larger, more complex societies. This was likely facilitated by increased agricultural productivity and trade enabled by iron tools.
  • The Painted Grey Ware culture, associated with the early Iron Age, is characterized by distinctive pottery and iron tools found across North India.
  • In the later period, we witnessed the rise of powerful Mahajanapadas, competing states that laid the foundation for larger empires like the Mauryas and Guptas.

questions.question: Ram and Ramesh can do a work in 12 days, Ramesh and Somesh in 15 days and Somesh and Ram in 10 days. If Ram, Ramesh and Somesh work together, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.questionHtml: Ram and Ramesh can do a work in 12 days, Ramesh and Somesh in 15 days and Somesh and Ram in 10 days. If Ram, Ramesh and Somesh work together, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

Ram and Ramesh can do work together =12 days

Ramesh and Somesh can do work together = 15 days

Somesh and Ram can do work together = 10 days

Formula used:

Work = Efficiency × Time

Calculation:

Let the Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh can complete the work together in X days

One day work of Ramesh and Ram =  \({1\over12}\)

One day work of Ramesh and Somesh = \({1\over15}\)

One day work of Somesh and Ram = \({1\over10}\)

One day work of all three = \({1\over12}+{1\over15}+{1\over10}\) = \({5+4+6\over60}={15\over60}={1\over4}\)

Working twice they can complete the work in = 4 days

They can complete the work = 8 days

∴ The required result will be 8 days.

Alternate MethodCalculation:

Ram and Ramesh = 12 days

Ramesh and Somesh = 15 days

Somesh and Ram = 10 days 

LCM of (12,15, & 10)  = 60 units

Efficiency of Ram and Ramesh = 60/12 = 5 units

Efficiency of Ramesh and Somesh = 60/15 = 4 units

Efficiency of Somesh and Ram = 60/10 = 6 units

Efficiency of 2(Ram, Ramesh & Somesh) = 15 units(5 + 4 + 6)

Total Efficiency of  Ram, Ramesh & Somesh = (5 + 4 + 6)/2 = 7.5 units

Time taken by Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh together to complete the work:

Time = Total work / Total Efficiency

⇒ 60/7.5 = 8 days 

∴ Ram, Ramesh, and Somesh together will complete the work in 8 days.

questions.solution:
Given:

They give us a relation between speed and time.

Formula used:

\(Speed={Distance\over Time}\)

Calculation:

Let the distance of the first person be D and time will be T.

The second person cover the distance = 25% of D = \({25\over100}\times D={D\over4}\)

Time taken by second person = 3T

The speed of the first person = \({D\over T}\)

The speed of the second person = \({{D\over4}\over3T}={D\over12T}\)

The ratio of their speed = \({{D\over T}\over{D\over 12T}}={12\over1}\)

The speed of the first and second person = 12 : 1

∴ The required result will be 12 : 1.

A dishonest dealer sells articles at 15% loss on cost price.

Concept:

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Formula used:

\(P\%={SP-CP\over CP}× 100\)     Where, P = Profit, SP = Selling price, and CP = Cost price

Calculation:

Let the cost price of the 25 g article be X.

The selling price of the article = \({(1\ -\ {15\over 100})}\ × X={({100-15\over100})}\ × X={85\over100}\ × X=0.85X\)

The cost price of the 20g article = \({X\over 25}\ × 20={4X\over5}\)

The profit percentage = \({0.85X-0.8X\over0.8X}× 100={0.05X\over 0.8X}× 100={0.0625\ × 100}=6.25\%\)

∴ The required result will be 6.25% Profit.

questions.question: ABC is a triangle and D is a point on the side BC. If BC = 16 cm, BD = 11 cm and ∠ADC = ∠BAC, then the length of AC is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: ABC is a triangle and D is a point on the side BC. If BC = 16 cm, BD = 11 cm and ∠ADC = ∠BAC, then the length of AC is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In ΔABC, if a point D lies on BC such that ∠ADC = ∠BAC, then AC is the geometric mean of BC and CD.

Given: BC = 16 cm and BD = 11 cm ⇒ CD = 16 − 11 = 5 cm.

Using the property: AC2 = BC × CD

AC2 = 16 × 5 = 80

AC = √80 = 4√5 cm.

∴ The correct answer is 4√5 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: BC = 16 cm, BD = 11 cm, and ∠ADC = ∠BAC.

Formula Used: AA Similarity Criterion (If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, the triangles are similar).

In ΔADC and ΔBAC:

⇒ ∠ADC = ∠BAC (Given)

⇒ ∠ACD = ∠BCA (Common angle)

⇒ ΔADC ∼ ΔBAC (By AA similarity criterion)

Since the triangles are similar, their corresponding sides are proportional:

⇒ AC / BC = CD / AC

⇒ AC2 = BC × CD

⇒ CD = BC − BD = 16 − 11 = 5 cm

⇒ AC2 = 16 × 5 = 80

⇒ AC = √80 = 4√5 cm

∴ The correct answer is 4√5 cm.

Additional Information

AA Similarity Criterion

Two triangles are similar if two corresponding angles are equal. This leads to the proportionality of all corresponding sides.

Geometric Mean in Triangles

In a triangle where an interior angle equals the opposite whole angle, the shared side acts as the geometric mean: Side2 = Segment × Whole Side.

Ratio of Areas

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides: Area(Δ1) / Area(Δ2) = (s1 / s2)2.

⇒ 6x - 24 + 4x - 40 + 3x = 144

⇒ 13x = 144 + 40 + 24

⇒ x = 208/13 = 16

Thus, time taken to complete the work = x = 16 days

questions.question: If the third proportional of 3x 2 and 4xy is 48, then find the positive value of y.
questions.questionHtml: If the third proportional of 3x<sup>2</sup> and 4xy is 48, then find the positive value of y.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For two terms A and B, the third proportional is given by B2 ÷ A.

Given: A = 3x2, B = 4xy, and the third proportional is 48.

Formula: (4xy)2 ÷ 3x2 = 48

⇒ 16x2y2 ÷ 3x2 = 48 ⇒ 16y2 ÷ 3 = 48 ⇒ y2 = 9 ⇒ y = 3 (since y is positive).

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

First term (A) = 3x2

Second term (B) = 4xy

Third proportional (C) = 48

Formula Used:

If A, B, and C are in continued proportion, then:

A ÷ B = B ÷ C

⇒ B2 = A × C

Calculations:

⇒ (4xy)2 = 3x2 × 48

⇒ 16x2y2 = 144x2

Since x is non-zero, we can divide both sides by x2:

⇒ 16y2 = 144

⇒ y2 = 144 ÷ 16

⇒ y2 = 9

⇒ y = √9

⇒ y = 3 (taking positive value as requested)

∴ The correct answer is 3.

Additional Information

Third Proportional

The third proportional of two numbers A and B is a value C such that A : B = B : C, which simplifies to C = B2 ÷ A.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two quantities A and B is given by √(A × B).

Fourth Proportional

If A, B, C, and D are in proportion (A : B = C : D), then D is the fourth proportional and is calculated as (B × C) ÷ A.

questions.question: The length of a hall is 21 m and the width is 14 m. The sum of the areas of the floor and the flat roof is equal to the sum of the areas of the four walls. Find the height of the hall.
questions.questionHtml: The length of a hall is 21 m and the width is 14 m. The sum of the areas of the floor and the flat roof is equal to the sum of the areas of the four walls. Find the height of the hall.
questions.solution:
Let the height of the hall be H

Area of floor = 21 × 14 = 294 m2

Sum of floor and ceiling = 588 m2

Area of four walls = 2 × (21 + 14) × H = 70H

70H = 588

H = 588/70 = 8.4 m
